content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an approach to de-bias the vision transformers in class incremental learning setting. They bring to additions to the transformer. 1) A logit adjustment strategy to de-bias the transformer towards the current classes by putting emphasis on the previous task classes. The idea comes from that each incremental phase is viewed as a long tail distribution, and a logit offset can reduce the inherent bias towards new classes. 2) Dual Distillation strategy to maintain the attention cast on the input image. This new transformer model can adaptively learn new task distributions without expanding the model parameters as the number of tasks grow. The idea comes from that preserving the spatial attention response of a model via distillation can help in improving the spatial awareness of the model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- By two additional mechanism, the proposed approach outperforms the existing methods.
- The model parameters don't grow as the number of tasks grow. 
- It doesn't require a big memory.

Weaknesses:
- The work proposed is incremental and the contribution is limited. For example it is not clear to me why the authors replaces ViT with NesT and why it is stated as a contribution? In addition, attention map matching distillation loss has been used in incremental learning.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The problem and the motivation of the paper is explained well. The algorithm is also clearly explained and it is easy to follow the paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed approach is simple but it outperforms the existing methods. It is well written, but the contribution is limited.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper addresses the problem of incremental learning, by introducing a transformer-based architecture called Debiased Dual Distilled Transformer (D^3Former). The model is built based on ViT Nest, which is a hybrid Transformer and CNN architecture. For the purpose of incremental learning, D^3Former includes a dual distillation (between attention maps and features produced by current and previous models) and debiasing through logit adjustment.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The method is technically sound.
- Good improvements are achieved compared with the baselines on datasets like CIFAR100 and ImageNet.

Weaknesses
- On the technical side, the paper lacks innovation for the following reasons. (1) Distillation is widely used as a regularization to avoid forgetting in the literature. Feature distillation is a very common technique in incremental learning to avoid forgetting (eg, Hou et al., 2019). Attention distillation is a natural choice for the transformer. Since Grad-CAM is also used, perhaps it is also applicable for pure CNN models. The Debiasing is simply borrowed from Menon et al., 2021. Hence, the technical innovation is quite limited. 
- There is a large body of literature in continual learning, but only the classical old ones and very few other ones are compared. There are many recent progresses in the context showing strong performance. More comparisons should be included in the comparison. Otherwise, it is hard to tell how strong the performance is. 
For example, [A] Hung et al, Compacting, Picking and Growing for Unforgetting, Continual Learning, NeurIPS 2019; [B]Mallya et al, Piggyback: Adapting a Single Network to Multiple Tasks by Learning to Mask Weights, ECCV 2018; and many others. A more thorough check on the literature is perhaps needed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The writing is generally easy to follow.
- Novelty is limited as discussed above.
- Code is provided as supplementary material.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I think the paper presents a reasonable method for incremental learning, which is a well-studied problem, but the proposed method is more or less a combination of a few existing methods. Further, considering the size of the incremental learning literature and the actual compared methods in the paper, it causes a bit of uncertainty on how strong the presented performance actually is. Hence, I lean to recommend rejection.

content.summary_of_the_paper: To research the capabilities of ViTs in class incremental learning (CIL), this work applies the Nested Vision Transformer (Zhang et al., 2022b) in CIL and proposes two key modifications (debiased classification loss and the dual distillation loss) to alleviate the class imbalance problem and minimize catastrophic forgetting in CIL, respectively, wherein the work combines the logit adjusted cross-entropy loss (Menon et al., 2021) and the cosine normalized classifier (Hou et al.,2019) to build the debiased classification loss while the dual knowledge distillation losses are used to preserve the orientation of the extracted features and keep the gradient-based class activation maps (Grad-CAM) consistent between the old and new models to transfer the old knowledge.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: It is meaningful to research ViT in incremental learning and it is interesting to keep the gradient-based class activation maps (Grad-CAM) (Selvaraju et al., 2019) consistent to preserve the response on regions that are critical for predicting a particular class to transfer the old knowledge, which helps to relieve catastrophic forgetting.
Weaknesses: 
(1) The novelty is not enough because: a) the debaised classification loss is an incremental novelty as the logit-adjusted cross-entropy classification loss and consine-normalized classifiers have already been proposed; b) The attention map matching distillation loss has been applied in incremental learning, for example <Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting with Hard Attention to the Task, ICML 2018>. There have been some previous works to research ViT in CIL/CL, such as <Continual Learning with Lifelong Vision Transformer, CVPR, 2022>. 
(2) The experiments are not enough to support some key claims of the paper for example, a) To validate the effectiveness of the debaised classification loss, there should be an ablation study comparing the debaised classification loss with the logit-adjusted cross-entropy loss and the cosine normalization classification loss or the regular cross-entropy loss; b) To validate the dual distillation losses, there should be ablation study of replacing the dual distillation losses with the regular logit distillation loss while keeping the other components unchanged. The paper lacks these experiments to support the effectiveness of the components of the algorithm C) It is better to conduct some visualization experiments to show that L_cam really helps to preserve the model response on regions that are critical for predicting a particular class.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The motivation is clearly stated, the algorithm is clearly stated, and easy to understand. 
Novelty: The novelty is not enough (See weaknesses).
Quality: The research is not robust enough, because the experiments are not enough to support some key claims of the paper (See weaknesses).
content.summary_of_the_review: This work researches and applies ViT in CIL by combining some extant techniques such as the logit-adjusted CE loss, and attention-based loss to render ViT to the setting of CIL. It is interesting to keep the gradient-based class activation maps (Grad-CAM) (Selvaraju et al., 2019) consistent to preserve the response on regions that are critical for predicting a particular class. But the novelty maybe not be enough for publication in ICLR and the research of this work is not robust because experiments are not enough to support some key claims of the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper addresses the problem of class incremental learning with Transformer architecture.
The authors claim that class incremental learning can be cast as a long-tail learning problem, where the data from old tasks are rare and the data from the new task is sufficient.
The paper proposes Debiased Dual Distilled Transformer ($D^3Former$), which leverages NesT with the proposed dual distillation and logit adjustment.
The goal of logit adjustment is to preserve the representations relevant to old tasks, and the goal of dual distillation is to maintain the configuration of attention maps.
The experimental results on various benchmarks show the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- Strengths
    - Casting the problem of incremental learning to a long-tail problem is reasonable and the idea of debiasing the logits seems to be an adequate solution.
    - At the same time, the proposed framework shows better performance than other baselines for the standard benchmarks.
    - The paper is well-written and clear.
- Weaknesses
    - My major concern for this work is a limited contribution.
        - Even though the proposed framework has some novel points, solving the incremental learning as the long-tail problem, “dual-distillation” is not novel at all to be claimed as a contribution. Dual-distillation, which consists of feature-level distillation and attention distillation, is the combination of previously studied concepts. **Feature-level distillation was first proposed by [Hou et al., 2019] and Grad-CAM distillation was studied by [Dhar et al., 2019].**
    - **Replacing ViT with NesT backbone** is just a choice of the backbone network, and cannot be considered a novel contribution. While the paper states that hybrid ViT models are more successful than pure self-attention-based ViT in terms of accuracy and cost, it’s the contribution of NesT paper, not this submission. It seems not fair to use NesT as the backbone compared to Dytox, since the initial performance of NesT is better than ViT. Or, it will be better to show that the proposed framework also effectively works with ViT backbone. Even though the authors show that the proposed objective terms work with ResNet backbone in Table 8,  it does not make the quality of the paper better since using distillation losses for ResNet is previously studied as mentioned above.
    - In the first item of contribution, the paper states that the proposed model outperforms DER [Yan et al., 2021] and RPS-Net [Rajasegaran et al., 2019] “as shown in Figure 1”. However, both works are not presented in Figure 1. I understand that the experimental setting of RPS-Net is different from other methods in Figure 1. However, the paper does not provide a comparison with DER [Yan et al., 2021], for the entire paper. Thus the sentence should be revised.
    - Discussion about Mixup and data used for distillation
        - According to the experimental results, D^3Former works well on CIFAR-100 without Mixup and without new samples for distillation. And I have three questions about the results.
            - First, how did you compute class priors mentioned in Eq (1), when Mixup is performed upon two classes, especially when one came from the old classes and the other came from the new classes?
            - Second, in Table 5, there is no result for all samples without Mixup. The mixup procedure between new classes and old classes might harms the training, especially for the debiasing loss. Thus, the result for distillation with all samples without mixup is needed to support the claim. Moreover, to be honest, I’m not sure how much the conclusion, which is **“distillation loss is indeed adding strong regularization for these small scale datasets”**, made in section 4.3.4 is related to the presence of mixup.
            - Third, for imageNet, the authors both used Mixup and all samples for distillation. The paper states that such difference comes from the number of learnable parameters in section 4.3.3. However, for me, the effect of data used for distillation might be more crucial to the ratio between the number of the old classes and the number of new incoming classes, rather than the size of the datasets. It will be nice if authors provide their opinion about this, or the ablation study for both datasets.
    - Minor
        - Repeated reference : [Wu et al., 2019a] and [Wu et al., 2019b] are the same.
        - Need consistency for the term “long-tail” and “long tail””

content.title: $\textrm{D}^3\textrm{Former}$: Debiased Dual Distilled Transformer for Incremental Learning
content.TL;DR: Adapting a hybrid ViT for class incremental learning
content.abstract: In the class incremental learning (CIL) setting, groups of classes are introduced to a model in each learning phase. The goal is to learn a unified model performant on all the classes observed so far. Given the recent popularity of Vision Transformers (ViTs) in conventional classification settings, an interesting question is to study their continual learning behaviour. In this work, we develop a Debiased Dual Distilled Transformer for CIL dubbed $\textrm{D}^3\textrm{Former}$. The proposed model leverages a hybrid nested ViT design to ensure data efficiency and scalability to small as well as large datasets. In contrast to a recent ViT-based CIL approach, our $\textrm{D}^3\textrm{Former}$ does not dynamically expand its architecture when new tasks are learned and remains suitable for a large number of incremental tasks. The improved CIL behavior of $\textrm{D}^3\textrm{Former}$ owes to two fundamental changes to the ViT design. First, we treat incremental learning as a long-tail classification problem where the majority samples from new classes vastly outnumber the limited exemplars available for old classes. To avoid bias against the minority old classes, we propose to dynamically adjust logits to emphasize on retaining the representations relevant to old tasks. Second, we propose to preserve the configuration of spatial attention maps as the learning progresses across tasks. This helps in reducing catastrophic forgetting by constraining the model to retain attention on the most discriminative regions. $\textrm{D}^3\textrm{Former}$ obtains favorable results on incremental versions of CIFAR-100, MNIST, SVHN,  and ImageNet datasets.
